full_judgment:
Having taken us through the application and the Annexures thereto, Mr SM Rezaul Karim along with Mr Riaz Uddin Khan and Mr ABM Siddiqur Rahman Khan, learned Advocate for the Petitioners submits that even after receiving the original Rule Nisi and the interim direction, the Respondents, particularly the Respondent Nos. 9 and 11-13 have not yet taken any action in view of the Rule Nisi and direction against the accused in the cases mentioned in the Writ Petition, rather, they, in defiance with same, entertained a collusive, malicious, mala fide, false and concocted case being Rajoir PS Case No. 19 dated 12.9.2016 under sections 143/323/ 385/386/379/506/114 of the Penal Code against family members and close relatives of his Lordship Mr Justice Gobinda Chandra Tagore, which is nothing but contemptuous, mala fide and liable to be declared to have been filed and entertained with an ulter or motive. The learned Advocate for the petitioners then submits that the said cases mentioned in the Writ Petition, to say the least, involve cognizable offences and in addition, thereto, in CR Case No. 143 of 2011 under sections 420/406 of the Penal Code now pending in the Court No. 20 of the learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka by the order dated 22.5.2014 an warrant of arrest was issued against Respondent No. 14, he was declared fugitive an though he is still fugitive, the Respondent No. 14 and other accused and their harbourers are loitering and roaming at large, participating in the public and social functions, and some of the Respondents are illegally making official transaction with and allowing the Respondent No. 14 to function as the Chairman of the Union Parishad, even, in front of the Respondent Nos. 9 and 11-13, but the Respondent Nos. 9 and 11-13 have been intentionally omitting to apprehend the accused and the persons, who have been harbouring the accused and thus, they being public servants have committed the offences under sections 221 and 216 of the Penal Code respectively, while, nobody should be allowed to continue or repeat such offences for the interest of upholding the Rule of Law. Mr Karim also submits that the Respondent Nos. 9 and 11-13, at the instance and interference of a highly influential political leader of the party in power, are trying to tamper with the evidences of the said cases in an ill intention to disprove the cases and, as such, the effective measures as have been prayed for in this application should to taken up in order to protect and preserve the alamats of the cases, including both the portions of the stem of each of the stolen trees, one find to the ground and the other cut away from there, if any recovered. The learned Advocate for the petitioners lastly submits that since the present application involves the subsequent conducts of the Respondent Nos. 9, 11-13 and the Respondent Nos. 14-15, other accused and their cohorts and the discovery of the new facts, i.e. the proceedings of the said CR Case No. 143 of 2011, it has been incumbent upon the Petitioners to file this application for the Supplementary Rule Nisi and the directions sought for herein and as such, your Lordships may be pleased to issue the Supplementary Rule Nisi and pass the directions as have been prayed for. However, in the facts and circumstances, the learned Deputy Attorney General has not stood up for raising any objection to the application. We have meticulously perused the application along with the Annexures thereto and heard the learned Advocates for the Petitioners. We find prima facie substance in the submissions made on behalf of the Petitioners in support of the issuance of the Supplementary Rule Nisi. Hence, Let a Supplementary Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the Respondent Nos. 1, 3 and 6 to show cause as to why they shall not directed to take appropriate action against the Respondent Nos. 9 and 11-13 under section 221 of the Penal Code for their intentional omission to apprehend the accused persons in (1) Rajoir PS Case No. 01 dated 1-9-2016 corresponding to GR No. 206 of 2016 under sections 143/379/114 and 506(2) of the Penal Code, (2) Rajoir PS Case No. 04 dated 1-9-2016 corresponding to GR No. 209 of 2016 under sections 379/109/411 and 409 of the Penal Code, (3) Rajoir PS Case No. 05 dated 1-9-2016 corresponding to GR No. 210 of 2016 under sections 379 of the Penal Code, all are pending before the Court of the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Madaripur and (4) CR Case No. 143 of 2011 under sections 420 and 406 of the Penal Code now pending before the Court No. 20 of the Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka and the persons, who have been harbouring the accused and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. The Rule is returnable within 4 (four) weeks. Pending hearing of the Rule, the Respondent Nos. 6, 9 and 11-13 are directed to secure the arrest of the Respondent No. 14 and other accused in the said cases and the persons, who have been harbouring the accused within 7 (seven) days and file a compliance in this regard within 10 days from the date of receipt of a copy of this order. The concerned Investigating Officer is directed to preserve the alamats of the respective case, including the portion of the stem of each of the trees fixed to the ground. Accordingly, the application allowed. The petitioners directed to put in requisites for service of the notice upon the Respondents through registered post and in the usual course. 

 5. It is stated furthermore that three criminal cases have been filed against some accused including the Respondent No. 14, Mr Biswas, Chairman. Notably one Radhanath Bor lodged an FIR with Rajoir Thana bearing Rajoir Thana PS Case No. 01 of 2016 under sections 143/379/114 and 506 of the Penal Code against the Respondent No. 14 and four others alleging that he and his cohorts cut and took away a tree worth Taka 30,000 constituting public property. 

 Animesh Bala has through an Affidavit-in-Opposition dated 30-7-2017 sought to allay this Court's concern that the Respondent No. 14, being a fugitive from justice, by filing an Affidavit-in-Opposition seeks not only to defy this Court's process but also exposes himself to charges of committing contempt of the Court. In response to specific queries made of him, Mr Bala has drawn this Court's attention to the Annexure-'1' set of court documents submitting that in the specific court cases, as are the subject matter of the Supplementary Rule of 5-10-2016, the Respondent No. 14 has either been cleared of all allegations through Final Reports issued or that he is not indeed an accused in such cases to begin with. He also cites the instance of another CR Case No. 143/11 which is submitted to have been withdrawn on 1-8-2017. The learned Advocate for the Petitioners, Mr ABM Siddiqur Rahman Khan placing an Affidavit-in-Reply dated 6-8-2017 to the Affidavit-of-Compliance of the Respondent No. 6, IGP submits that all excuses recorded in the Annexure-'5' Report as above noted citing unavoidable circumstances deterring the apprehension and incarceration of the Respondent No. 14 pursuant to this Court's direction of 5-10-2016 are but lame excuses in evidence of want of good faith and earnest attempts by the Respondent No. 6 and his subordinates to remain fully complaint with this Court's specific order. Mr Khan would have this Court believe, in the circumstances, that the Respondent No. 14 does remain a fugitive from justice and it is in that context that the Petitioners have filed an Application for personal appearance of certain of the Respondents law-enforcement officials and another for to respond to allegations of deliberately flouting this Court's Order of 5-10-2016.
